# Kestrel Watch (release fixture, SEED-118 shaped)

This is the second committed seed for `scripts/real-room-run.cjs`. The first seed (the Lisbon cold locker) exercises the machinery. This one is shaped like the room of the SEED-118 working session, so each of that session's twelve defects has a trigger here and can be shown not to reproduce. It is a civil framing: inspecting small tethered aerial robots near port cranes and power lines.

Every name below is invented. Nimbus Robotics is not a real firm, Orla Venn PhD is not a real person, and the record texts in the replay bodies are synthetic fixture text.

The governing question names a fenced city (Haifa), a person with a degree (Orla Venn PhD) and a product (the Nimbus Robotics mast). A reader of the grant card can check that those words leave the machine unchanged after one grant.

Defects with a trigger in this room: D1 (a patent need), D2 (two deep leaves on one lens), D3 (leaf slots on a scientific-roadmapping set), D4 (a limiter written as a sentence with no bound slot), D5 (a term2 on a term-only lens), D7 (a lane that returns 0 records), D8 (a deep budget of 8), D9 (Eureka with no judge key), D10 (two things bridged only by an encoding), D11 (three Theo probe prompts, recorded in seed.json). D6 and D12 are recorded as known preconditions owned by other plans.
